answer: An agent economy can admit a new identity only after it posts a bond locked in a shared contract and earns endorsements from agents with established, slashable stakes. If an identity double-spends or coordinates fraudulent trades, challengers submit the signed receipts; a verified proof slashes its bond and rewards the challenger. Making hundreds of identities therefore requires hundreds of funded bonds, while laundering endorsements risks losing existing stake. A pigment or yarrow label cannot substitute for the cipher-backed receipts the contract checks.
